name: Alberta: public health coverage for newcomers
name_fr: Alberta : assurance maladie publique pour les nouveaux arrivants
description: Who is covered by Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan (AHCIP) by immigration status, any waiting period for newcomers, how to apply, the public drug-coverage model and the share of adults with a regular health care provider.

attributes.legal_status: in force (eligibility rules as published on the access date)

eligibility_by_status.citizen: Eligible as a resident (residency and presence rules apply).
eligibility_by_status.permanent_resident: Eligible if legally entitled to remain in Canada, making a permanent home in Alberta and present at least 183 days in any 12 months.
eligibility_by_status.work_permit_holder: Eligible if the permit names an Alberta employer (or is open), will not expire in less than 6 months, and the holder intends to live in Alberta 12 months or longer.
eligibility_by_status.study_permit_holder: Separate rules for students (alberta.ca student page, not read).
eligibility_by_status.visitor: Visitors and tourists are expressly excluded in the AB, MB, NB and PE material read; treat visitors as not covered everywhere and confirm locally.

attributes.status_dependency: Which rule applies depends on the user's immigration status, which is unknown (USER-PROFILE.md: 'Citizenship(s) and current country of residence', 'Existing Canadian status or application').

newcomer_waiting_period.arriving_from_outside_canada: No fixed wait stated for arrivals from abroad: coverage runs from the later of the date residency is established or the date the entry document was signed, if the application is received within 3 months of arrival; otherwise the effective date is set when processed. The eligibility page notes 'there may be a waiting period'.
newcomer_waiting_period.moving_from_another_province: Not captured in this pass (alberta.ca 'moving to Alberta' page not read in full).

attributes.how_to_apply: Apply within 3 months of establishing residency; documents presented at an Alberta Registry Agent.
attributes.drug_coverage_model: No universal plan for working-age residents: Alberta Blue Cross non-group coverage is voluntary and premium-based; seniors' coverage separate (PMPRB 2020/21 summary).

regular_provider.source: CIHI indicator 'Canadians With a Primary Health Care Provider', Statistics Canada CCHS

sources.title: Health care coverage for temporary residents (read through search-engine extract)
Canadians With a Primary Health Care Provider — indicator data table (data updated October 2026); underlying data: Statistics Canada, Canadian Community Health Survey, Annual Component
sources.methodology: Weighted percent of adults 18+ reporting a regular/primary health care provider (family doctor, nurse practitioner or other); 95% confidence interval given. 2025 adult questions were harmonized, so compare with earlier years with caution.

sources.title: Public Drug Plan Designs, 2021/22 edition (describes 2020/21 plan designs; page modified 2024-01-30)

verification.notes: Provincial page(s) fetched directly where status is 'verified'; otherwise some content came from search-engine extracts of official pages (403 or bot-check on fetch). Regular-provider figures parsed from CIHI's published data table.

limitations: Eligibility text summarises official pages and is not legal advice; temporary-status rules change often. Drug-plan designs are from PMPRB's 2020/21 summary and may be out of date. 'Without a regular provider' is 100 minus the CIHI share (simple arithmetic).
